title.en: How Spain's migrant crisis created a political storm - whipped up by social media
title.zh: 西班牙移民危机如何在社交媒体煽动下引发政治风暴

summary.en: The Ceuta crossings have politically shaken Europe, exposing deep divisions over the sensitive issue of migration, a BBC report indicates. Social media has played a role in intensifying the political storm surrounding these events.
summary.zh: 英国广播公司报道称，休达边境的移民潮在政治上震动了欧洲，暴露了在敏感的移民问题上的深刻分歧。社交媒体在加剧围绕这些事件的政治风暴中发挥了作用。

body.en:
Most of the tens of thousands of migrants who swam into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Thursday have now returned to Morocco, escorted to the border by Spanish soldiers and police.

But the extraordinary surge of arrivals has left at least 67 people dead, their bodies pulled from the sea where they floated alongside abandoned rubber rings and flippers.

This week's events have also shaken Europe politically, once again exposing divisions over the sensitive issue of migration.

And they've left lingering questions about what sparked the sudden influx: whether social media posts promising an easy path to Europe just went viral or this was something more deliberate, even organised.

Whatever the cause, Spain's socialist prime minister is angry with the response.

Pedro Sanchez has hit out at some in the EU for "attacking" Spain in this crisis, playing politics instead of showing support.

Fratelli d'Italia, the hard-right party of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, had been quick to post images of migrants racing through the streets of Ceuta.

"This is the Sanchez model the Italian left wing likes so much," the caption crowed.

Meloni then announced she was suspending Italy's Schengen agreement with Spain that allows for the free movement of people, citing a security threat.

The way Spain sees it, the crisis has been contained and Ceuta is not in the Schengen zone so Moroccan migrants were never going to head for mainland Europe, unchecked.

But she faces elections next year with her coalition losing ground to a new and virulently anti-immigrant party. This was a chance to sound tough herself and claw back votes and she leaped on it.

Meloni's call for an urgent meeting of interior ministers to be held on Tuesday was signed by almost two dozen EU heads of state, calling for the elimination of all policies that could be "pull factors" to Europe.

Above all, they mean Spain's controversial move to allow hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants apply for residence and work permits and "regularise" their status.

But those who flocked to the beaches of Ceuta this week were not heading to sign up for a campaign that's already closed.

Sanchez himself points instead to a recent ruling by Spain's Supreme Court: it said those who enter by sea cannot be pushed back immediately.

The prime minister argues that was misrepresented by smugglers to promise an easy path to Europe.

The crowd heading for Ceuta didn't need to pay smugglers, though, because most were Moroccan and the route is well known.

Migrants have shown social media posts to reporters with people shouting that "Spain is Open" and jumping into the sea.

body.zh: 周四涌入西班牙飞地休达的数万名移民中的大多数现已在西班牙士兵和警察的护送下返回摩洛哥。 但涌入的人数激增，导致至少 67 人死亡，他们的尸体与废弃的橡胶圈和脚蹼一起漂浮在海面上。 本周的事件也在政治上震动了欧洲，再次暴露了在敏感的移民问题上的分歧。 他们留下了一个挥之不去的问题，即是什么引发了突然涌入的人潮：社交媒体上承诺通往欧洲的便捷道路的帖子是否只是病毒式传播，还是这是经过深思熟虑、甚至有组织的。 无论出于何种原因，西班牙社会党首相都对这种反应感到愤怒。 佩德罗·桑切斯猛烈抨击欧盟一些人在这场危机中“攻击”西班牙，玩弄政治而不是表示支持。 意大利兄弟会（Fratelli d'Italia）是总理乔治亚·梅洛尼（Giorgia Meloni）领导的极右翼政党，该党很快就发布了移民在休达街道上奔跑的照片。 “这就是意大利左翼非常喜欢的桑切斯模式，”标题欢呼道。 梅洛尼随后宣布，她以安全威胁为由，暂停意大利与西班牙允许人员自由流动的申根协议。 在西班牙看来，危机已经得到遏制，而且休达也不在申根区，因此摩洛哥移民永远不会不受限制地前往欧洲大陆。 但她面临明年的选举，她的联盟将输给一个新的、恶毒的反移民政党。这是一个让自己听起来强硬并夺回选票的机会，她抓住了这个机会。 梅洛尼呼吁周二召开内政部长紧急会议，这一呼吁得到了近二十位欧盟国家元首的签署，呼吁取消所有可能对欧洲产生“拉动因素”的政策。 最重要的是，他们指的是西班牙允许数十万无证移民申请居留和工作许可证并“规范”他们的身份的有争议的举措。 但本周涌入休达海滩的人们并不打算报名参加已经结束的活动。 桑切斯本人则提到了西班牙最高法院最近的一项裁决：该裁决称，不能立即将通过海路入境的人驱逐。 首相辩称，走私者歪曲了这一点，承诺提供一条通往欧洲的便捷道路。 不过，前往休达的人群不需要付钱给走私者，因为大多数是摩洛哥人，而且路线众所周知。 移民向记者展示了社交媒体帖子，人们高喊“西班牙开放”并跳入海中。 我们检查过的多个账户显示，年轻人穿着潜水衣和脚蹼，或者拍摄自己已经游泳的样子，混合着……

reflection.en: The political storm surrounding migration in Europe, amplified by social media, highlights the challenge of welcoming those seeking refuge. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to treat foreigners as native-born, loving them as ourselves, recalling our own shared human experience of being strangers. This principle calls for compassion and unity amidst the...
reflection.zh: 欧洲围绕移民问题引发的政治风暴，在社交媒体的推波助澜下，凸显了接纳寻求庇护者的挑战。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，要善待寄居者如同本地人，爱他们如同爱自己，因为我们都曾是异乡客。这一原则呼吁我们在复杂的社会问题所造成的隔阂中，展现出怜悯与合一。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
title.zh: 秘鲁旅游飞机坠毁，13人遇难

summary.en: A small tourist plane crashed while flying over the Nazca Lines archaeological site in Peru, resulting in the deaths of 13 people.
summary.zh: 据当地报道，一架小型旅游飞机在秘鲁纳斯卡线条考古遗址上空飞行时坠毁，造成13人死亡。

body.en:
A small plane carrying tourists has crashed in Peru, killing all 13 people on board, according to local news reports and Peruvian officials.

The aircraft, a Cessna Caravan C-208, had been flying over Nazca Lines ​archaeological site when it went down on Saturday. Eleven passengers and two pilots were on board.

The passengers included two German, two Spanish and seven Italian tourists, Peru's state news agency reported. The cause of the crash is not yet clear.

The Nazca Lines is a popular tourist attraction and Unesco World Heritage site in southern Peru that features ancient drawings of animals in desert sand. Tourists often fly in small planes to see the extent of the drawings.

"Given the severity of the accident, there are no survivors. We have recovered four bodies so far," Police Major Jorge Andrade said, according to AFP.

The crash happened around 13:00 local time (19:00 BST) in the Pueblo Viejo region after the plane departed from an airport in Pisco, Peru.

Video from Reuters news agency shows firefighters spraying water at the scene as smoke rises from the wreckage.

In a statement in Spanish posted online by the Municipalidad Provincial de Nasca, officials expressed "deep sorrow" for the accident and extended "heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased".

In a statement, the airline said it would "assess its flight schedule in accordance with the directives of the relevant authorities", according to Reuters.

This isn't the first plane to crash over the famed site in the past few decades.

In 2022, another small tourist plane crashed during a flight over the Nazca Lines site, killing seven on board.

And in 2010, a tourist plane went down over the site, killing six people on board.
body.zh: 据当地新闻报道和秘鲁官员称，一架载有游客的小型飞机在秘鲁坠毁，机上 13 人全部遇难。 周六坠毁时，这架飞机正在飞越纳斯卡线考古遗址。机上有十一名乘客和两名飞行员。 纳斯卡线是秘鲁南部一个受欢迎的旅游景点，也是联合国教科文组织世界遗产，以沙漠中的古代图画为特色。 据法新社报道，警察少校豪尔赫·安德拉德说：“鉴于事故的严重性，没有幸存者。到目前为止，我们已找到四具尸体。” 飞机从秘鲁皮斯科机场起飞后，于当地时间 13:00 左右（英国夏令时 19:00）在普韦布洛维耶霍地区发生坠机事故。 纳斯卡省市政厅在网上发布的一份西班牙语声明中，官员们对这起事故表示“深切哀悼”，并向死者家属表示“衷心哀悼”。 这并不是过去几十年来第一架在这个著名地点坠毁的飞机。 2022 年，另一架小型旅游飞机在飞越纳斯卡线遗址时坠毁，造成机上 7 人死亡。 2010年，一架旅游飞机在该地点上空坠毁，机上六人丧生。

reflection.en: The sudden loss of life in this tragic accident brings profound sorrow. In moments of such unexpected grief, we remember that even Yahweh, in the person of Jesus, wept at the death of a friend. This simple act reminds us that it is right to mourn and that our pain is seen.
reflection.zh: 这场悲剧性事故中生命的突然逝去带来了深切的悲痛。在这样意想不到的悲伤时刻，我们记得，即使是雅伟，以耶稣的身份，也曾为朋友的离世而哭泣。这个简单的举动提醒我们，哀悼是恰当的，我们的痛苦是被看见的。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Moscow restaurant bombing kills three people as device carried by woman explodes

The explosion occurred just before 8pm close to an Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow’s seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinskaya ​Square, the police said. Continue reading...

reflection.en: Acts of violence like this bombing remind us of the pervasive presence of evil in the world and the profound suffering it inflicts. In such moments, Yahweh calls us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively seek ways to overcome evil with good, fostering peace and healing where destruction has occurred.
reflection.zh: 此次爆炸等暴力行为提醒我们，世间邪恶无处不在，并造成深重苦难。在这样的时刻，雅伟呼召我们不要被邪恶所胜，而是要积极寻求以善胜恶的方式，在破坏发生之处培育和平与医治。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja among 10 killed in Pakistan avalanche
title.zh: 尼泊尔著名登山家 Nirmal Purja 在巴基斯坦雪崩中遇难 10 人之一

summary.en: Purja and nine others were caught in an avalanche on Broad Peak, with rescuers yet to retrieve their bodies.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Celebrated Nepali climber Nirmal Purja, who set a record for the fastest ascent of the world's 14 highest mountains, died in an avalanche during an expedition in Pakistan, his company said on Saturday.

"Today it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak, his expedition organising company Elite Exped said in an Instagram post.

"We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive," it added.

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said he was stunned at the deaths of the climbers, including Purja.

"Only physical journey of the climbers has stopped. But the history of their courage, dedication and contributions will always remain alive and inspiring," Shah wrote in a social media post.

Purja, 43, and nine others had been missing since Thursday after being struck by an avalanche on the 8,051-metre Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest mountain, a technically difficult climb in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region.

Officials said the bodies of Purja and other climbers were located in a difficult site and had yet to be retrieved.

Purja, who served in the British military with the Gurkhas and later in special forces, completed his record-breaking feat in six months in 2019.

He became widely known internationally after the Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible," was released two years later.

UK defence minister Wes Streeting said he was "incredibly" sad to learn of the death of Purja and the other climbers.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over," Streeting wrote on X.

The 10 mountaineers were caught in an avalanche around midday on Thursday. Six of them were Nepalis, and the others were from ⁠Pakistan, Oman, the US and China.

Chhang Dawa Sherpa, a board director of Seven Summit Treks, which had three Sherpa guides among the dead ⁠climbers, said the remaining bodies were "spotted and identified" with the help of drone footage and were yet to be retrieved.

"They are in a difficult spot and have not been retrieved yet," Chhang told Reuters news agency.

He said that unlike Nepal, Pakistan does not have the practice of long-line rescue by helicopters on the mountains.

"We have to take into account the safety of those who go and retrieve the bodies."

title.en: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say

summary.en: Security officials said a woman tried to enter the restaurant with explosives but was stopped by a security guard.

body.en:
At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media quotes security officials as saying.

The blast happened at around 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre.

The National Anti-Terrorist Committee (NAK) said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the restaurant.

The restaurant, located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, had been holding a private function.

Authorities have not disclosed the guest list or said anything about who they believe was the target of the attack.

Witnesses said they saw people being brought out covered in blood after the explosion.

Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside".

Roads around the square were briefly closed. Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride through the city but the event was cancelled.

Video released by Russia's RIA news agency showed heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to members of the public.

In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around the Russian capital. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for those attacks.

title.en: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
title.zh: 孤独作为一种新的理想生活方式：“我们并不孤独”

summary.en: A growing number of what the internet has dubbed "loneliness influencers" are spotlighting solo living without children or friends - and it's spurring debate.

body.en:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video – which has amassed seven million views on TikTok – is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.

For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

After switching several high schools, enduring Covid isolation during her college years and moving across the country following her first heartbreak, Isa found herself forced to adjust to living alone with no close friends.

"People don't talk about having no friends a lot... I think it's still what people would consider embarrassing or a little taboo," she says.

When she started sharing the friendlessness of her circumstances on social media, an audience began to connect. Her initial following of around 2,000 followers on TikTok swelled to more than 175,000 in the span of eight months.

"It was eye-opening to see other people who are living the same situation that I've been… and to feel like I could kind of relate to people for the first time in a while."

And relate they did. Isa's comments section filled with people bonding over similar experiences of living alone or having no friends, and finding comfort in "feeling seen".

As with most trends online, curiosity quickly turned to backlash. Isa and similar creators were dubbed "loneliness influencers", with some framing them as part of a new demographic of sad, lonely, childless women in crisis.

Others accused them of romanticising self isolation and encouraging an "air of cosy defeatism" by shunning social connections.

title.en: Young guns for hire - the teenage hitmen recruited to kill across Europe
title.zh: 欧洲各地招募青少年杀手——“小枪手”

summary.en: The Foxtrot Network is reportedly responsible for approximately 35 murders across Europe, employing a "violence-as-a-service" model that involves recruiting teenagers as hitmen.
summary.zh: 据报道，狐步舞网络在欧洲各地实施了大约35起谋杀案，该组织采用“暴力即服务”模式，招募青少年充当杀手。

body.en:
In a Stockholm suburb a man dressed in black appeared out of the winter night. Carrying a handgun, he approached 20-year-old Murad Abdelkader, a student on his way back from a shift at McDonald's.

The gunman opened fire, shooting again and again as he approached his target. He fired the last shot into his victim's head as he lay helpless on the ground.

The killer was 18-year-old Atilla Azimov. On that February night last year, he had killed the wrong man.

He had done it for money - hired by the Foxtrot Network, an organised crime group with links to the Iranian regime which has become notorious for its violence-as-a-service (VaaS) tactics.

Since 2022, the Foxtrot Network is thought to have been responsible for about 35 murders as well as a number of attacks and attempted attacks on Israeli targets in Europe including two involving explosives and hand grenades.

The gang recruits teenagers to carry out the attacks for cash, but it almost never has to pay out as they often get caught.

Like Johannes Natland, a Norwegian teenager who was convicted of conspiracy to murder by a jury at the Old Bailey in London on Wednesday for a planned killing in West Yorkshire.

According to Operational Taskforce (OTF) GRIMM, the Europol group set up to tackle the problem, the teenage hitmen are recruited on social media, and are given their instructions in a "gamified" way, imitating how computer games work.

Andy Kraag, the head of Europol's European Serious and Organised Crime Centre, calls it the "calculated outsourcing of murder" to vulnerable young people.

OTF GRIMM currently involves 11 countries affected by the VaaS phenomenon - Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom.

The leader of the Foxtrot Network, Rawa Majid, has fled Sweden and his later operating base in Turkey, and is now based in the Iranian capital Tehran. Police believe some of the VaaS attacks have been carried out for the Iranian regime, including a hand grenade attack on the Israeli embassy in Copenhagen, though other attacks are part of Foxtrot's drugs turf wars.

Diamant Salihu, an investigative journalist for the Swedish broadcaster SVT, has been researching Foxtrot and its Iranian links for three years.

"The regime is ordering the leader of the Foxtrot Network to instigate his network to commit attacks against the Iranian regime's enemies," he said.

"It can be dissidents, journalists that are in the opposition against the regime, and it can also be Israeli targets."

The links to the Iranian regime started after October 2023 when Majid fled to Tehran, Salihu said.

Spanish authorities have begun installing a 500-metre floating barrier on its border with Morocco in the enclave of Ceuta in north Africa after a mass rush of migrants killed at least 67 people.

It comes as the European Union held crisis talks after more than 50,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta on Thursday. Most had returned to Morocco within 48 hours.

Reuters video on Saturday showed Spanish soldiers and police patrolling a mostly empty Tarajal beach shrouded in fog.

Spanish Civil Guard police started laying the new barrier at 7.50am local time on Saturday (3.50pm AEST) on the Tarajal breakwater, one of the main points used by people trying to enter the tiny Spanish territory, the government said in a statement.

The barrier, alongside a line of anchored naval buoys, is designed to stand 30 to 70 centimetres above water and extend as much as one metre below the surface, it added, while a channel between the barriers will allow Civil Guard vessels to patrol the area.

The mass crossing prompted alarm across the European Union, and 22 member states wrote a letter asking for coordinated action to protect external borders and other measures.

Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, said it had called an emergency video conference meeting of the bloc's interior ministers to discuss the crisis on Tuesday.

Spain's centre-left Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez criticised Italy's decision on Friday to suspend passport-free Schengen travel arrangements with Madrid for one month.

"In the current international context, the EU cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction," Sanchez wrote in a letter to the EU Commission and European Council presidents.

At least 67 bodies have been recovered on the Spanish side of the frontier, officials said, after some migrants drowned and others were crushed while trying to climb the breakwater and border fence.

Many were driven to migrate by economic hardship and encouraged by social media rumours.

Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska blamed people-smuggling networks for exploiting vulnerable migrants and spreading misleading interpretations of a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling that migrants intercepted at sea cannot be summarily returned in the absence of a physical barrier.

Speaking from Ceuta, Grande-Marlaska told reporters Spain had largely restored order within 24 hours, but warned that the crisis was not yet formally over, and that reinforced police and military deployments would remain as long as needed, though overnight crossings had fallen to about zero.

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement officers sealed off the area and launched an investigation.

Russia has faced several attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. They blamed a ‌series of assassinations and attempted killings on Kyiv.

title.en: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
title.zh: 东欧如何纪念罗姆人大屠杀？

summary.en: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?

It took decades before Germany recognized the Romani Holocaust — the Nazi genocide of 500,000 European Roma and Sinti during World War II . Several more decades passed before the European Holocaust Memorial Day for Sinti and Roma became an official German and European day of remembrance, celebrated each year on August 2.

Based on initiatives by Polish Roma groups, the Nazi liquidation of the so-called "Gypsy Family Camp" in the Auschwitz-Birkenau Concentration and Extermination Camp on the evening of August 2-3, 1944, was first commemorated half a century later, in 1994. 

Thousands of deported Roma and Sinti had already been killed as a result of malnutrition and disease. That evening, thousands more were forced into gas chambers, shot and beaten to death by Nazi henchmen.

In 2015, the European Parliament declared this date the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany and other European countries, the genocide is commemorated by officials with the participation of government representatives. In some cases, representatives of European governments travel to the memorial site in Auschwitz.

In most cases, however, countries hold their own memorial services — particularly in central and southeastern Europe, where Nazi extermination commonly targeted Romani peoples . These days, such memorial days also take the opportunity to raise awareness for ongoing Antiziganism and the consequences it has. 

Poland , home to an estimated 30,000 Roma, has been observing August 2 since 2011. The ceremony routinely includes a visit by parliamentary and governmental representatives to the Auschwitz Memorial.

Another important day of remembrance is observed each year in the village of Szczurowa, east of Krakow, on July 3. It honors the memory of Polish Roma massacred by German troops in 1943. In 1956, Szczurowa became the first site of a European memorial for victims of the Romani Holocaust.

Other small towns and villages across southeastern Poland also commemorate the killing of Polish Roma during Nazi German occupation. 

In the Czech Republic , where nearly 250,000 Roma live, August 2 has been an official day of remembrance since 2015. The most important ceremony is held in Lety, south of Prague, where Roma organizations have been commemorating the genocide for decades. This is the site where German Nazis established a concentration camp in 1940, and began deporting and imprisoning Romani families from occupied Bohemia from 1942 onward.

title.en: Russia pummels Ukraine as Zelenskyy begs allies for better air defences

summary.en: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has issued a warning that Ukraine's US Patriot air defense systems have depleted their interceptor missile supplies, amidst ongoing heavy bombardment from Russia.

body.en:
Russia pounded Kyiv in a heavy ballistic missile attack on Saturday, killing nine people, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukraine had run out of interceptor missiles for its US Patriot air defence systems.

Zelenskyy said Russia launched 35 missiles at Ukraine, including 27 ballistic missiles, and 185 drones. Only one ballistic missile was intercepted, "simply because there are no interceptors for the Patriot system", he said.

More than a dozen explosions reverberated through the city during several waves of attacks, according to Reuters news agency witnesses.

"Every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves the lives of our people. And every night without them results in more casualties," Zelenskyy said on the Telegram messaging app.

With the war in its fifth year, fighting is raging along roughly 1,200 kilometres of front line. But Russian advances have slowed by more than half this year, and Ukraine has been launching strikes inside Russia, hitting its oil facilities, logistics sites, and weapons production.

At the same time, Russia intensified its attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, while Ukraine is chronically short of air defences capable of downing ballistic missiles, which travel at several times the speed of sound.

Moscow and Kyiv both deny targeting civilians in the war launched by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Saturday's is the second major attack on Kyiv this week after strikes on Thursday killed nine people, including six members of one family in a village near Kryvyi Rih , and a suspected Russian cruise missile landed in Poland.

Damage was recorded in seven districts across Kyiv, a city of about 3 million people, the Prosecutor's General Office said after Saturday's attacks.

Zelenskyy said that fires broke out across Kyiv and 18 residential buildings, a school, the Lithuanian Embassy, and infrastructure facilities were damaged.

The Lithuanian foreign ministry said windows at its embassy had broken, solar collectors were damaged, and the yard was scattered with debris.

Ukrainian prosecutors said seven people were killed in the Darnytskyi district on the left bank of the Dnipro river and two more people died in the Solomyanskyi district on the right bank of the city.

Dozens of people were injured, including four children who suffered multiple shrapnel wounds and lacerations.

Zelenskyy had met with US President Donald Trump on Wednesday for talks, partly to lobby Washington for licenses to produce Patriots domestically.

title.en: War in Ukraine: Why Crimea has become a strategic target
title.zh: 乌克兰战争：克里米亚为何成为战略目标

summary.en: Ukraine has intensified its attacks on Russian logistics and energy facilities in Crimea, raising questions about the impact on local supplies and Kyiv's strategy to influence the war's trajectory.
summary.zh: 乌克兰加强了对克里米亚俄罗斯后勤中心和能源设施的袭击，引发了关于对当地供应的影响以及基辅希望通过此战略改变战争走向的疑问。

body.en:
Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian logistics centers and energy facilities in Crimea. What are the consequences for local supplies, and how does Kyiv hope this strategy will affect the course of the war?

In an attempt to isolate Crimea  from the mainland, the Ukrainian armed forces have intensified their attacks on the peninsula, which was invaded and annexed by Russia in 2014.

Ukraine is using long-range drones to attack transports on the M14 highway between the Russian city of Rostov-on-Don and Melitopol in occupied southern Ukraine. It is also targeting Russian shadow fleet ships in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea , as well as energy facilities that supply the Russian military.

Robert "Magyar" Brovdi, commander of the Ukrainian forces for unmanned systems, says 196 Russian ships and more than 100 energy facilities have been hit in the past month alone. His figures cannot be independently verified.

Russia appears to be struggling to supply both its military and the civilian population in Crimea. Fuel coupons were issued at the end of May, but ran out after 24 hours, after which gasoline was being traded on the black market. A state of emergency was declared in Crimea, especially Sevastopol, in response to repeated disruption of the electricity and water supply, and of the internet and cellphone networks.

Nina, a pensioner who lives in a village near Feodosiya, southeastern Crimea, told DW about the difficulties people there are facing: Residents there can't cook because of power cuts, and fuel shortages mean public transport only runs intermittently. Nina's worst fear, though, is not having electricity in winter.

The longest power cuts have been in the north of Crimea. This is where Ivan lives [name changed]. He tells DW that for some time, people were unable to get hold of fuel with either coupons or cash. The only exceptions, he says, were police officers, state officials, and doctors. For several days, everything collapsed: Cars ran out of fuel and simply came to a stop; people didn't know how they were supposed to get to where they were going.

Ivan said that most shops no longer stock perishable goods, because they can't run their fridges and freezers: "There are no milk products, or fish, or meat," he said. "There are only a few shops with electricity generators, but the prices there are much higher than before."

Some small, private, volunteer initiatives are trying to help. The blogger Olena Gerasimenko works with companies in Simferopol to bring drinking water to people suffering from power cuts, and to hospitals and kindergartens. In her blog, she reports that people are complaining about the lack of help from the Russian-installed "authorities" in Crimea.

title.en: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
title.zh: 加密货币矿工如何在东南亚窃取电力

summary.en: Illegal cryptocurrency miners across Southeast Asia are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.
summary.zh: 东南亚各地，非法加密货币矿工正在窃取大量电力，这不仅给国家电网带来压力，也暴露出与有组织犯罪的联系。

body.en:
Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids, and exposing links to organized crime.

A raid in Malaysia last week exposed how  cryptocurrency mining is becoming entangled with electricity theft and organized crime across Southeast Asia.

In Malaysia's southern state of Johor, 71 cryptocurrency-mining machines had been running around the clock across four rented premises for about a month before police moved in.

During the raids on July 22 and 23, officers arrested three suspects and seized computers, routers and vehicles alongside equipment used to illegally mine Bitcoin . 

Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad said the syndicate bypassed electricity meters, leading to an estimated €14,500 ($16,600) in losses in about a month, according to local media reports. The machines were thought to be generating between €17,200 and €21,500 in monthly revenue.

The case was relatively small by Malaysian standards. Between 2020 and 2025, national utility Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) identified almost 14,000 premises linked to electricity theft for cryptocurrency mining. Its cumulative losses reached around €1.1 billion.

Recorded cases of such theft increased from 610 in 2018 to 2,397 in 2024, according to Malaysia's Energy Ministry, which has described illegal mining as a serious threat to public safety, economic stability, and the national electricity system.

"In Malaysia, thousands of incidents have triggered investigations into illegal mining for cryptocurrency purposes," said Sonny Zulhuda, associate professor at the International Islamic University Malaysia.

"This poses a huge problem for the security of electricity resources, economic sustainability, competition, and revenue loss," Zulhuda told DW. "Enforcement has been lagging behind, due to a lack of legislative preparedness and limited agency capability in enforcement and investigation. This is unfortunate because Malaysia is fast developing its digital infrastructure."

Cryptocurrency mining is not inherently criminal, but authorities are increasingly finding links between illegal crypto mining, online gambling, money laundering, and Southeast Asia's industrial-scale cyber scam networks .

Last October, the United States and the UK sanctioned the  Cambodia -based Prince Group and associated companies, alleging that the network operated forced-labor scam compounds and laundered proceeds through cryptocurrencies and other assets.

US authorities also seized Bitcoin worth around $15 billion at the time from wallets whose private keys were held by Prince Group chairman Chen Zhi , describing the cryptocurrency as proceeds and instruments of fraud and money laundering.

title.en: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance
title.zh: 英国法院批准中国“超级”大使馆建设计划

summary.en: A UK court has dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which is set to become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, had cited security concerns regarding the embassy's presence.
summary.zh: 英国一家法院驳回了针对中国驻伦敦新大使馆的法律挑战，该大使馆建成后将成为英国最大的使馆。此案由一个社区协会提起，理由是该大使馆构成安全威胁。

body.en:
A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

A UK High Court on Friday threw out a challenge against UK authorities' decision to permit a new Chinese super embassy in central London .

The challenge was brought by a neighborhood group called the Royal Mint Court Residents' Association (RMCRA), which represents families and businesses in roughly 100 properties around the planned embassy site.

The RMCRA argued the presence of the embassy could increase the risk of terrorist attacks, lead to the targeting of dissidents and be used to enforce "draconian" Chinese laws in the UK.

The association also claimed that the embassy could pose a fire risk, arguing that Chinese authorities might ignore safety obligations that would be difficult to enforce because of diplomatic immunity on the embassy site.

On that basis, the group argued the development should not have been approved by the UK government as well as the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.

Yet in its ruling on Friday, the High Court said the "RMCRA ​did not produce reasonable ⁠and convincing evidence of the likelihood that a violation of human rights ⁠affecting them ​personally would occur."

In a move that was widely seen as a goodwill gesture toward Beijing, the embassy received approval from the UK government shortly before then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited China in January this year. 

 If completed, the new Chinese embassy would be the largest embassy in the UK .

Beijing plans to build the embassy on the site of the former Royal Mint, next to the Tower of London. The site covers around 20,000 square meters (235,000 square feet).

Beijing purchased the property in 2018 for a reported $327 million (€283.9 million), with the intent of relocating its embassy there from its current premises in Portland Place.

In response to the verdict, the RMCRA said it would seek permission to appeal, hoping to take the case to the UK Supreme Court.

"Beijing thinks this judgment is the final word. It isn't. The appeal is already in the works," Luke Pollard, head of the RMCRA, said in a statement.

Activists from  Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement living in exile have also been skeptical of the project, telling DW they fear the embassy could help Beijing suppress dissidents abroad. 

The UK is home to the world's largest Hong Kong diaspora, with an estimated 285,000 people of Hong Kong origin living in the country.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

This verse reminds us that all our labor, when done with diligence and integrity, can be an offering to Yahweh, giving it enduring purpose beyond economic shifts. Even as job roles evolve, the dignity of human contribution...

How can AI remain safe, accountable and under human control ? How should its development be governed? How can its benefits be shared more widely? Continue reading...

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the names and images of Indigenous persons who have passed away.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country to legislate a social media ban for children under the age of 16.

While the jury is still out on its effectiveness , the laws introduced world-first penalties for social media giants that are caught breaking the rules.

Now, a range of countries — including Britain, France and Malaysia — look set to follow suit, something that Australian policymakers have taken as a point of pride.

In late June, the prime minister's office put out a statement saying Australia had "started a global movement". Anthony Albanese himself said the nation was "leading the world".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's not the first time Australia has led the charge on ambitious legislation and inventions.

Lucie Shawcross — who has researched Australian ingenuity and inventiveness at the National Archives of Australia (NAA) — believes "there are just so many incredible [Australian] inventions out there that have made an impact globally".

"Spray-on skin is an Australian invention, the cochlear implant, WiFi," the exhibitions curator told SBS News. "There are some really profound inventions that have impacted upon all of us."

Other distinctly Australian inventions that have seen mass uptake include the dual flush toilet, Hills Hoist, the baby capsule, Aerogard and cask wine (also known as goon ), according to the NAA.

In 2012, Australia took the radical step of removing all branding from cigarette packaging, replacing it instead with plain packaging, public health warnings and confronting images of smoking-related illnesses.

The policy, introduced under Julia Gillard's Labor government, was designed to make smoking less "cool" — or, as Gillard herself wrote in The Guardian in 2013, "kill the glamour and substitute it with the facts: smoking equals death".

The move was widely opposed by cigarette companies who unsuccessfully sued the Australian government over the changes.

By 2016, plain packaging was included in guidelines to the World Health Organisation Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

Now France, the UK, New Zealand, Norway, Ireland, Thailand, Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, Israel, Slovenia, Türkiye, Canada, Singapore, Belgium, the Netherlands and Georgia have all adopted similar policies.

Laws requiring motorists to use seatbelts are almost taken as natural now, but that wasn't always the case — Victoria became the first jurisdiction in the world to make seat belts compulsory in 1970.

body.en:

The approach to North Sullivan's home is a magical journey through winding eucalypt-lined roads, where traffic signs warn of wombats and roaming horses greet passing cars.

The driveway to the 71-year-old's home — aptly named Wombat Gully — is situated on the doorstep of Yengo National Park, part of the World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains area, around two hours north-west of Sydney.

His property is one of 22 clustered in what they call Upper Yango, on the site of a former dairy farm that was subdivided into small hobby farms.

Sullivan says the landholders were a "very disparate community" prior to the Black Summer fires of 2019-20.

But friendships were formed as they fought side-by-side to protect their properties.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

From the ashes of that traumatic experience emerged an enduring lesson: one of the most valuable assets in an emergency are the people around you.

The community is now one of many across Australia taking direct action to reduce the risks of fire and flood, as climate change is projected to increase the frequency and severity of such extreme weather events.

Since the fires, the Upper Yango community has developed wide tracks that double as firebreaks in strategic locations, as well as other measures to reduce fire risk to their properties.

However, Sullivan says these efforts are not reflected in their insurance premiums.

He is just one of many landowners SBS News has spoken to in NSW who are either struggling to find insurance cover or facing rising costs.

Some experts warn the pressures could leave some communities unviable, with implications that extend beyond remote and regional Australia.

As premiums continue to rise and access to cover becomes more challenging, communities are questioning whether efforts to reduce disaster risk will be enough to keep insurance affordable.

Professor Paula Jarzabkowski, an expert on insurance protection gaps at the University of Queensland, says there's already significant evidence that many Australians are struggling to get adequate cover for their properties — either because it's too expensive or because policies exclude specific risks, like certain types of flood or fire.

"Brisbane is built on a floodplain, parts of Sydney are built on floodplains, so we have seen catastrophic flooding in these major cities as well," she tells SBS News.

title.en: Brian is turning some visitors away from his farm — and he's not the only one
title.zh: 布赖恩正在谢绝一些访客进入他的农场——他不是唯一一个这样做的人

summary.en: Across Australia, some farmers are implementing measures to safeguard their birds, with one farmer, Brian, reportedly turning visitors away from his property.
summary.zh: 在澳大利亚各地，一些农民正在采取措施保护他们的禽类。据报道，一位名叫布赖恩的农民甚至谢绝访客进入他的农场。

body.en:
For 60 years, Brian Ahmed has farmed the same stretch of land in Melbourne's east. These days, getting past the farm's gate isn't easy — his birds need all the protection they can get.

"At the moment, because of all the concerns with Avian influenza ... I'd say all farms now have increased their biosecurity levels," he told SBS News.

"Our number one priority is to protect our birds, and the best way we can do that is to make sure they don't mix with anyone that they don't need to."

Avian influenza, or bird flu, is a highly contagious virus that predominantly affects bird species, causing severe disease and sudden death.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It has wreaked havoc on avian and mammal species in other parts of the world, but until recently hadn't made it to mainland Australia.

The disease now appears to be spreading across the country quickly , with 53 confirmed or presumed cases nationwide, just a month after the first contagious bird was found.

The latest figures were confirmed on Saturday, with the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry saying a silver gull found at Robe in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu — the first confirmed detection in a silver gull in Australia.

Experts indicate that the recent detection is important, as gulls move between beaches, wetlands, farmland, and urban areas, potentially spreading the virus to wider environments.

At the same time, in Victoria, preliminary testing has identified five crested terns, three from Portland and two from Nelson Bay, suspected to have bird flu.

Farmers across the country have been encouraged to take precautions, something that might impact their operations.

Chris Groves, chairman of the farming systems committee with the National Farmers Federation, told SBS News that "agricultural industries really have to take their precautions, their biosecurity, to the next level".

"It will cause some interruptions to daily operations of a large poultry farm because they have to be more careful," he said.

"A lot of the big operators, they've prepared for this already. They've dealt with and seen what happened with the other strain of bird flu that we did have in Victoria. So it won't cause a big hiccup in the industry at all there."

There  have been no detections in poultry or in Australia's agricultural production system.

National leaders met on Friday to discuss Australia's ongoing response to the virus, which now spans five states.

Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said they vowed to do "everything we can" to help protect Australia's wildlife, agricultural industries and the national economy amid the outbreak.

title.en: El Niño is already here. But there's still a 'window of opportunity'
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象已至，但仍有“机会之窗”

summary.en: The El Niño climate pattern has arrived and is projected to be one of the strongest ever recorded, prompting questions about its potential impacts on Australians.
summary.zh: 厄尔尼诺气候模式已经到来，预计将成为有记录以来最强的一次，引发了人们对其可能对澳大利亚人造成影响的疑问。

body.en:
As El Niño strengthens, now is the "window of opportunity" to prepare before its potential impacts unfold, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned.

The United Nations agency said El Niño is continuing to intensify and is expected to strengthen from August to October in a new long-range forecast released Saturday.

El Niño typically peaks between November and February, with its greatest influence on global temperatures often felt in the following year.

It's expected to drive up the likelihood of higher-than-normal temperatures across many parts of the world, increasing the risk of drought in some regions and wetter conditions in others.

"El Niño is not just on our doorstep — it is inside the house and turning up the heat," UN Secretary-General António Guterres said.

"And this is only a warm-up act. El Niño is strengthening — adding fuel to a planet already on fire with scorching heat domes, apocalyptic wildfires and record hot seas."

The World Food Programme is seeking to protect 8.8 million people across 22 high-risk countries before weather patterns "escalate into humanitarian emergencies". It expects parts of Africa, Central America and East Asia to be the most at risk.

In Australia, El Niño increases the likelihood of warmer and drier conditions, particularly in the east and southeast, raising the risk of drought and bushfires.

The Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) declared El Niño underway in mid-June, and forecasts it will be a "very strong event" — perhaps among the strongest observed since 1950 — that may persist into autumn next year.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo urged people and leaders around the world to consider the potential risks to their communities and take action.

"El Niño is one of the most closely monitored climate phenomena in the world," she said.

"This El Niño developing against the backdrop of unprecedented ocean heat and rising temperatures, provides governments and communities with a window of opportunity to anticipate risks and act before impacts unfold."

An El Niño declaration can be particularly concerning for farmers and those in bushfire-prone regions.

While it doesn't guarantee hotter and drier conditions, it does raise the probability that they will occur.

Andrew King, an associate professor of climate science at the University of Melbourne, said that while this El Niño is likely to be one of the strongest on record, a strong El Niño does not necessarily have a huge bearing on Australian climate compared to a weak one.

title.en: 'Mirage': Voice architect Noel Pearson breaks silence at Garma on referendum defeat
title.zh: “海市蜃楼”：原住民“议会之声”提案设计者诺埃尔·皮尔逊在加尔马节打破公投失败后的沉默

summary.en: Noel Pearson, a key architect of the proposed Indigenous Voice to Parliament, has delivered his first major public address since the referendum's defeat nearly three years ago, speaking at the Garma festival.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚原住民“议会之声”提案的主要设计者诺埃尔·皮尔逊在公投失败近三年后，首次在加尔马节上发表重要公开讲话。

body.en:
Noel Pearson, the architect of the failed Voice to Parliament 2023 referendum, has given his first major public speech in three years at this year's Garma Festival, Australia's largest Indigenous cultural gathering .

"For those of us who urged faith, hope and love, there is an account to be given for the hopes raised, the faith urged and the love lost in the referendum," he said.

"I must account for that. Three years later, I stand here with great reluctance.

"What right has anyone to raise hopes when those hopes were so badly misplaced? What right has anyone to offer a vision that turns out to be a mirage? That is the source of my hesitation to speak of these things. But I cannot allow the failure of the referendum to excuse me from my responsibility."

Nearly three years have passed since just over 60 per cent of Australians voted against enshrining an Indigenous Voice in the constitution, with every state and territory except the ACT rejecting the proposal.

Pearson, co-founder of the Cape York Land Council, was a prominent "Yes" campaigner at the time.

In his speech on Gumatj Country in the Northern Territory, he showed a map of where the majority of voters voted yes or no, with "blue dots" showing locations voting in favour of the referendum.

"The discrete Indigenous communities of Australia, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, overwhelmingly wanted the Voice. The rest of the country did not," he said.

"Fifty kilometres from my blue-dot home is the orange-dot township of Cooktown. Captain Cook spent six weeks there in 1770. I was born in its hospital. In 2023, Cook's town voted 'no'."

According to an estimate by political analyst Simon Jackman, in areas where Indigenous Australians made up the majority of the population, 63 per cent voted "Yes".

"From the very beginning of my public life, it was, and still is, the future of those communities, not least my own, that has been the central focus of my wakeful dreams," Pearson said.

"Our present is not good. And nor is our future assured. The things that worried me when I was 22 now distress me at 61.

"When I was 22, I worried because we knew something needed to be done, but we did not yet know how to do it. Now, we are much clearer. We know what we need to do. We know what we want to do."

Pearson added the "blue dot communities", communities voted in favour of the referendum, "stand in grave need of healing".

"There is no better solution to healing individuals, families and communities than guaranteed work," he said.

"They will start to heal. They will start to grow. They will start to strengthen.
